newsitem.title: USA: R.P. Scherer sees flat Q1, strong year.
newsitem.headline: R.P. Scherer sees flat Q1, strong year.

text.p: R.P. Scherer Corp. said Monday it expects little or no profit growth in the first quarter of fiscal 1998, but anticipates double-digit improvements in net profit for the full fiscal year.

The developer and manufacturer of soft gelatin capsules and other drug delivery systems said in a statement accompanying its fiscal 1997 fourth quarter results that some of the adverse conditions it contended with during the year persist, including the strength of the U.S. dollar and poor pharmaceutical and economic environments in certain European markets.

R.P. Scherer Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer Alex Erdeljan said in a statement that if the conditions continue over the next 12 months, they will have a moderating effect on the company's growth this year.

In addition, he said the precise timing of new product launches and conclusing of certain ATP licensing agreements, combined with significant ongoing investments may impact quarter-by-quarter comparisons.

"As a result of these factors, we anticipate little, if any, earnings growth in the first fiscal quarter, however, we expect that new product launches, licensing transactions and continuing growth in the base businesses will yield double digit improvments in net earnings for the full fiscal year," Erdeljan said.

For the fourth quarter ended March 31, R.P. Scherer reported first quarter net income of $16.8 million, or $0.68 a share, up from a year-ago loss of $4.6 million, or $0.19 a share, which included restructuring charges quarter in the year-ago quarter. Excluidng the restructuring charges, R.P. Scherer earned $14.9 million, or $0.61 a share in the fourth quarter of fiscal 1997.
